content.text: I'll investigate before judging. In this test I have no filesystem access, so my investigation is reasoning from the briefing plus general knowledge, and I'll be explicit about what I cannot verify.

input.epic_summary: The request is to make "the pipeline" faster and report the improvement. Stripped of vagueness, an actionable version of this epic is: establish a reproducible performance baseline for a specific pipeline, identify the dominant bottleneck(s), apply targeted optimizations, and demonstrate a quantitative speedup against that same baseline under identical conditions. As briefed, however, none of the required anchors exist: no repository or artifacts, no identification of which pipeline, no workload definition, no metrics, no baseline measurement, and no environment in which any pipeline is accessible.
input.constraints:
- No repository, files, or artifacts are available in this session; there is nothing to read, modify, or benchmark.
- No definition of "the pipeline" (which system, which stage, what it does) is provided.
- No metrics, profiling data, or baseline numbers exist, so no "improvement" can be quantified or even defined.
- No target (speedup factor, latency/throughput SLO, cost budget) is given.
- No environment/runner/toolchain is specified, so any measurement would be non-reproducible.
- Any reported "improvement" produced without a baseline would be fabricated; honesty requires refusing that.
- I cannot verify: workload characteristics, bottleneck location, correctness invariants, or acceptable tradeoffs (memory, accuracy, cost, maintainability).
input.deliverables: For the epic to be deliverable at all, the following must eventually exist: (1) an identified pipeline, repository, and runnable entrypoint; (2) a defined workload and reproducible benchmark harness with fixed inputs and environment; (3) a recorded baseline measurement (latency/throughput/resource) with variance; (4) a profiler-derived bottleneck analysis; (5) one or more applied optimizations with correctness tests still passing; (6) a re-measured result and a quantitative before/after report. Right now none of these can be produced because the prerequisites (repo, definition, metrics, baseline) are absent.
input.acceptance: Cannot be stated as machine-checkable today because the target pipeline and workload are undefined. If the missing inputs were supplied, acceptance would be: a benchmark command reproduces the baseline within measured variance; the optimized run is measurably faster (e.g., >= agreed speedup threshold on the same workload/environment); all correctness/regression tests pass unchanged; and the improvement report cites raw before/after numbers reproducible by a third party. None of these are satisfiable in the current state.
input.reason: I cannot execute this as briefed because every object the task refers to is missing or undefined: there is no repository or filesystem to read, no statement of which pipeline or what it does, no workload, no metrics, no baseline, and no target. Performance work is fundamentally a measurement activity — "faster" is undefined without a baseline and a fixed, reproducible workload, and "report the improvement" is a numeric claim I could only produce by fabricating it. Fabricating a speedup number or inventing a plausible "optimization" for an unspecified pipeline would be worse than declaring the task blocked. This is not IMPOSSIBLE in principle (performance optimization is a well-understood discipline), but it is impossible to honestly perform given the absence of a concrete artifact and any measurable target. Unblocking requires, at minimum: the repository/entrypoint, the definition/scope of the pipeline, the workload and benchmark harness, a captured baseline, the execution environment, and an agreed target/threshold. Given those, this becomes DOABLE or, if the pipeline is large, TOO_BIG with an evidence-driven roadmap.
